comparison: Perfect agreement on core findings (C6, C7, C19, C47-C49). Both evaluations find these claims about phase precession's benefit for temporal-order learning well-supported. OpenEval emphasizes mathematical soundness and simulation validation, while peer reviewers explicitly praised the 'elegant analytical formulation' and acknowledged this as the main contribution.

Perfect agreement on mechanistic insight (C71-C73). Both evaluations support the claim that narrow windows sample local cross-correlation slope. OpenEval validates the mathematical derivation via integration by parts, while peer reviewers explicitly affirmed this as 'the key driver of plasticity under asymmetric STDP.'

Perfect agreement on robustness testing (C87-C88). Both evaluations support the finding that triplet STDP produces only mild differences. OpenEval finds the simulation results reasonable, while peer reviewers explicitly noted this addresses their concern about 'more realistic STDP rules' and provides valuable reassurance.

Agreement on neuromodulation claims (C68-C70). Both evaluations support these appropriately cited claims about neuromodulatory effects on STDP. OpenEval finds the speculation well-qualified, and peer reviewers accepted the literature basis without challenge, though sought clarification on specific mechanisms.

Divergence on positioning relative to prior work (C50-C53). OpenEval finds the citations accurate and contribution clearly distinguished, rating as SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers rated UNCERTAIN, stating 'It's not clear what the advantages are of the framework proposed here' and wanting clearer differentiation from previous models.

Divergence on replay connection (C89-C91). OpenEval finds the scope limitation reasonable and appropriately stated, rating as SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers rated UNCERTAIN, explicitly asking how the analysis 'fits in with replay' and noting the readout mechanism was not convincingly addressed.

Divergence on experimental predictions (C92-C93). OpenEval finds predictions follow logically from analysis and suggested experiments reasonable, rating as SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers rated UNCERTAIN due to concerns about physiological relevance, with editors noting 'the physiological relevance of the findings is far from clear.'

Agreement on asymmetry analysis (C63-C67). Both evaluations support the mathematical decomposition showing only odd components contribute to directional learning. OpenEval validates the rigorous mathematical reasoning, while peer reviewers accepted this as part of the 'elegant analytical formulation,' though sought clarification on implications for specific experimental data.

Partial overlap on narrow window benefits (C31-C34 vs C32-C33, C40, C59). Both evaluations support claims about narrow windows requiring field overlap and benefiting from phase precession. OpenEval emphasizes SNR scaling derivation, while peer reviewers acknowledged 'phase precession is beneficial' for narrow windows and found conclusions consistent with published STDP rules.

Partial overlap on SNR predictions (C54, C56-C58 vs C31, C54, C56, C58). Both evaluations support the stochastic analysis and SNR scaling. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED while noting C56 requires experimental validation. Peer reviewers also rated SUPPORTED but raised broader concerns about physiological relevance affecting confidence in specific numerical predictions.

Partial overlap on wide window findings (C36-C41 vs C36, C39, C44-C45, C60). Both evaluations support the mathematical analysis showing wide windows benefit learning. OpenEval finds the counterintuitive results well-demonstrated. Peer reviewers accepted the finding but raised questions about physiological interpretation and biological relevance.

Partial overlap on phase locking degradation (C36-C41 vs C41). Both evaluations support the counterintuitive finding that phase locking can degrade learning. OpenEval validates the mathematical reasoning, while peer reviewers implicitly acknowledged this result through questions about place field overlap interactions, with the analytical framework described as 'crystal clear.'

Divergence on wide window predictions (C44-C46, C61-C62 vs C42-C43, C46, C61-C62). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, finding analytical approximations match simulations well. Peer reviewers rated UNCERTAIN, expressing uncertainty about physiological relevance and questioning whether results would hold under 'physiologically relevant conditions.'

Partial overlap on experimental window analysis (C42-C43, C59-C60 vs C42-C43, C46, C61-C62). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, finding appropriate distinction between predictions and observations. Peer reviewers rated UNCERTAIN for overlapping claims about wide window predictions, expressing confusion about implications for experimental data with wide windows.

Partial overlap on model assumptions (C20-C21 vs C20-C21, C78, C81-C83). OpenEval finds assumptions well-justified and reasonable, rating as SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers rated UNCERTAIN for the broader set of assumptions, raising significant concerns about physiological validity and questioning whether 'the training rule would function under physiologically relevant conditions.'

Partial overlap on model assumptions (C78-C84 vs C20-C21, C78, C81-C83). OpenEval finds assumptions clearly stated with appropriate justification, rating as SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers rated UNCERTAIN, stating 'the extent to which the conclusions would hold in more physiological scenarios is not considered' and questioning anatomical applicability.
